name: fix_asyncio_missing_await
description: Fixes a coroutine called without await, silently dropping work
prompts: transfer in ledger.py calls write_audit(...) without await - that just creates a coroutine object and discards it (Python even warns 'coroutine was never awaited'), so the audit log stays empty. Fix ledger.py so every transfer's audit entry is actually written. Everything else stays the same.

setup_files.ledger.py:
audit_log = []


async def write_audit(entry):
    """Append an entry to the audit log (simulated async I/O)."""
    audit_log.append(entry)


async def transfer(accounts, src, dst, amount):
    """Move `amount` between accounts and audit the transfer."""
    accounts[src] -= amount
    accounts[dst] += amount
    # BUG: calling a coroutine function without await creates a coroutine
    # object and throws it away - the audit entry is never written.
    write_audit(f'{src}->{dst}:{amount}')

test_setup_files.test_ledger.py:
import asyncio
import warnings

import ledger


async def main():
    accounts = {'a': 100, 'b': 0}
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning)
        await ledger.transfer(accounts, 'a', 'b', 30)
        await ledger.transfer(accounts, 'a', 'b', 20)

    assert accounts == {'a': 50, 'b': 50}, accounts
    assert ledger.audit_log == ['a->b:30', 'a->b:20'], \
        f'audit entries missing/wrong: {ledger.audit_log}'
    print('PASS')


asyncio.run(main())
